answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from work-bonded identity: every new agent locks a copper-backed deposit and publishes a cipher commitment to its first task before receiving it. The deposit is refunded only after two independent peers verify the work; a failed or copied job forfeits it. Each verified job grows a slow reputation score — like a walnut tree, it takes seasons to mature and cannot be bought in bulk. A sybil attacker must fund a fresh deposit and do verified work for every fake identity, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits and a thousand honest jobs.
